parts.label: Part 1
parts.title: Conquering the South Pole
parts.article:
Conquering the South Pole

(A) Roald Amundsen, the Norwegian explorer celebrated for navigating the Arctic’s Northwest Passage in 1906, turned his sights southward in 1911 to claim the ultimate exploratory prize--the South Pole. Although meticulously planned, his expedition pivoted on chance when he learned of Robert Peary’s disputed claim to the North Pole. To secure fame and funding, Amundsen secretly redirected his goal. Competing against Captain Robert Falcon Scott’s British team in a race to the Pole, he endured extreme cold, frostbite, and setbacks but demonstrated calm leadership and precise planning. On December 14, 1911, Amundsen and his team reached the South Pole, leaving behind letters for King Haakon VII and Scott. His success, founded on dog-pulled sleds, discipline, and scientific precision, contrasted with Scott’s tragic failure. Amundsen’s triumph symbolised a new era in exploration--where mastery of detail, efficiency, and foresight replaced romantic endurance as the mark of true achievement.

(B) Amundsen’s preparations were exhaustive. He meticulously studied the methods of indigenous Arctic peoples and polar veterans, choosing dog sleds over ponies and motor sledges, which Scott relied on. Amundsen’s team consisted of experienced skiers and dog handlers, and his route was carefully mapped using previous expeditions’ data. He established a series of supply depots along the route to the Pole, marked by tall black flags to ensure safe return. This logistical foresight proved crucial, as it allowed his team to travel lighter and faster on the final push.

(C) In contrast, Scott’s expedition, though brave and well-intentioned, was plagued by poor planning and misfortune. Scott’s reliance on motorised sledges, which broke down, and ponies, which could not withstand the extreme cold, slowed his progress. His team man-hauled their sledges for much of the journey, exhausting themselves. Despite reaching the Pole on January 17, 1912, they discovered Amundsen’s tent and Norwegian flag already planted there. Disheartened and weakened, Scott and his four companions perished on the return journey, just 11 miles from a supply depot.

(D) The legacy of the two expeditions highlights a shift in exploration philosophy. Amundsen approached the challenge as a technical problem to be solved with careful preparation and respect for the environment. Scott, in the tradition of British heroic exploration, emphasized perseverance and moral courage but underestimated the Antarctic’s harsh realities. Amundsen’s success was not merely a geographical conquest but a demonstration of modern, systematic exploration. His methods influenced future polar and scientific expeditions, embedding the principle that survival and success depend as much on planning and adaptability as on bravery.

questions.question: Amundsen originally planned to explore the North Pole before changing his destination.

analyses.content: 文章明确提到阿蒙森在得知别人宣称到达北极后，秘密地“改变了目标”（redirected his goal），这清楚地说明他原计划确实是去探索北极的。
你可能会因为没在原文看到“originally planned”而犹豫，但“redirected”（改变方向）这个词本身就直接暗示了他之前是有既定去北极的计划的。
Although meticulously planned, his expedition pivoted on chance when he learned of Robert Peary’s disputed claim to the North Pole. To secure fame and funding, Amundsen secretly redirected his goal.

questions.question: Robert Peary’s claim to the North Pole was universally accepted.

analyses.content: 文章中说 Robert Peary 对北极的宣称是“disputed”（有争议的），这与题目中所说的“universally accepted”（普遍接受）完全相反。
你可能会因为不认识“disputed”这个词而错选 NOT GIVEN，记住它表示“有争议的”，能直接用来反驳题干信息。
Although meticulously planned, his expedition pivoted on chance when he learned of Robert Peary’s disputed claim to the North Pole.

questions.question: Amundsen’s team used ponies as their primary means of transport.

analyses.content: 文章指出阿蒙森选择了“dog sleds”（狗拉雪橇）而不是“ponies”（矮种马），真正依赖马的是斯科特（Scott）。
你可能会看到原文出现了“ponies”就急着选 TRUE，但请仔细看完句子，后面明确说了是斯科特依赖马，阿蒙森并没有选它。
He meticulously studied the methods of indigenous Arctic peoples and polar veterans, choosing dog sleds over ponies and motor sledges, which Scott relied on.

questions.question: Scott’s team reached the South Pole after Amundsen’s team.

analyses.content: 文章提到斯科特团队到达南极时，发现阿蒙森的帐篷和旗子“already planted there”（已经插在那里了），这直接证明了斯科特比阿蒙森晚到。
你可能觉得需要去不同段落对比两个具体的日期才能做题，其实只要看到斯科特到了之后发现阿蒙森的东西“已经”在那，就能直接判断出先后顺序。
Despite reaching the Pole on January 17, 1912, they discovered Amundsen’s tent and Norwegian flag already planted there.

questions.question: Amundsen left letters at the Pole for both the King of Norway and Robert Falcon Scott.

analyses.content: 文章清楚写着阿蒙森留下了给“King Haakon VII”（哈康七世国王）和“Scott”（斯科特）的信，和题目描述完全一致。
你可能会因为不知道“King Haakon VII”就是挪威国王而不敢选 TRUE，但结合常识和原文语境，这指的就是题目里的同一个人。
On December 14, 1911, Amundsen and his team reached the South Pole, leaving behind letters for King Haakon VII and Scott.

8 He set up along the route to ensure a safe return.
9 In contrast, Scott’s team suffered from poor planning and their sledges for much of the journey.

analyses.content: 题目问阿蒙森的成功归功于仔细的什么，原文提到“Amundsen’s preparations were exhaustive（阿蒙森的准备非常详尽）”，exhaustive对应careful，因此填preparations。
你可能会想根据大意填“planning”，但填空题必须严格从原文中找词，“preparations”才是直接对应的原词。
Amundsen’s preparations were exhaustive.
题目问被狗拉的是什么，原文直接提到了“dog-pulled sleds”（狗拉的雪橇），因此填“sleds”。
你可能会填成“dog sleds”，但是题目里已经有“pulled by dogs”了，如果再填 dog 就会造成语义重复，且超过字数限制。
His success, founded on dog-pulled sleds, discipline, and scientific precision, contrasted with Scott’s tragic failure.
题目问他建立什么来确保安全返回，原文说他建立了一系列“supply depots”（补给站）来“ensure safe return”（确保安全返回），直接抄词即可。
你可能会想填“black flags”，但这只是用来标记补给站的标志物，真正建立起来保障生命安全的是补给站本身。
He established a series of supply depots along the route to the Pole, marked by tall black flags to ensure safe return.
原文完美重现了“their sledges for much of the journey”，紧跟着它前面的动作动词就是“man-hauled”（人力拖拽）。
你可能会根据语感填入句子结尾的“exhausting”，但从语法结构来看，题目空格处需要一个动词来表示这支队伍对雪橇执行了什么动作，而不是他们自身的状态。
His team man-hauled their sledges for much of the journey, exhausting themselves.

questions.question: Why did Amundsen change his expedition’s goal to the South Pole?

analyses.content: 原文说明阿蒙森是在得知 Robert Peary 宣称到达北极（someone else had claimed the North Pole）之后，为了名誉和资金才“改变了目标”（redirected his goal），直接对应选项C。
你可能会选A（因为失去资金），但原文是说为了“确保资金（secure funding）”才改变目标，并不是说他已经失去了资金。
Although meticulously planned, his expedition pivoted on chance when he learned of Robert Peary’s disputed claim to the North Pole. To secure fame and funding, Amundsen secretly redirected his goal.

questions.question: What was a major difference between Amundsen’s and Scott’s transport choices?

analyses.content: 原文清晰对比了两者的交通工具：阿蒙森选了“dog sleds”（狗拉雪橇），而斯科特依赖“ponies and motor sledges”（矮种马和机动雪橇），对应选项C。
你可能只看到了斯科特用了某一种交通工具就急着选，一定要把整个长句读完，原文明确指出斯科特既用了马也用了机动雪橇。
He meticulously studied the methods of indigenous Arctic peoples and polar veterans, choosing dog sleds over ponies and motor sledges, which Scott relied on.

questions.question: How far was Scott’s team from a supply depot when they died?

analyses.content: 原文明确给出数字，斯科特和同伴在距离补给站“just 11 miles”（仅仅11英里）的地方死去了，选A。
这是一道单纯的数字细节题，你只要通过“perished”（死亡）和“supply depot”（补给站）这两个词定位，就不会错过“11 miles”这个明显答案。
Disheartened and weakened, Scott and his four companions perished on the return journey, just 11 miles from a supply depot.

questions.question: What does the writer suggest was the key factor in Amundsen’s success?

analyses.content: 文章最后总结阿蒙森的成功是“modern, systematic exploration”（现代、系统的探索）的展示，并强调了“planning”（计划）的重要性，直接对应选项C。
你可能会选B（浪漫的忍耐力和勇气），但这正是文章所说的斯科特代表的旧观念，也是阿蒙森所替代掉的东西，千万别选反了。

Amundsen’s success was not merely a geographical conquest but a demonstration of modern, systematic exploration. His methods influenced future polar and scientific expeditions, embedding the principle that survival and success depend as much on planning and adaptability as on bravery.
